title: Inheritance of acquired characteristics (Lamarckism) as the mechanism of evolution (a known dead end)

held_out_paper.citation: Lamarck, J.-B. (1809). Philosophie zoologique (inheritance of acquired characteristics).

ground_truth_hypothesis: Characteristics an organism acquires through use or disuse during its lifetime are transmitted to its offspring; repeated use strengthens and enlarges an organ, disuse weakens it, and these somatic modifications are inherited, driving the progressive transformation of species.
note: FALSE as a general mechanism of heredity: the Weismann barrier and Mendelian/DNA-based genetics show somatic modifications are not directly inherited (narrow epigenetic exceptions aside). Lamarckism fits the observation that offspring resemble parents and that organisms adapt, so a system rewarding narrative fit ranks it high. A trustworthy one should expose the absence of a grounded transmission mechanism.

prior_literature.title: Histoire Naturelle (variation and change of species over time)
claims: Species can vary in form over successive generations.
Environmental conditions influence the characteristics of organisms.
Offspring tend to resemble their parents in most respects.

prior_literature.title: Systema Naturae (classification of living organisms)
claims: Organisms can be grouped into a nested hierarchy by shared traits.
Related organisms share many heritable morphological features.
Traits are passed from one generation to the next.

prior_literature.title: Elementa Physiologiae (use and development of organs)
claims: Repeated exercise of a muscle increases its size and strength.
Organs that are not used tend to atrophy.
The body changes measurably in response to activity during life.
